failure_summary.description: Bare list or pair of real people ('Ferdinand VII, Juan Carlos'; 'Princess Caroline & Princess Stephanie'; 'Finland, Norway, Sweden') answered with one member, a relationship word ('sisters') or a group label ('Nordic countries'). The key is the shared country or realm (Spain, Monaco).
Answer over-specified with extra words: 'Sea lamprey' for 'lamprey', 'Hallmark Cards' for 'Hallmark', 'Conan the Destroyer' for 'Conan' (it echoes the clue word 'destroyer').
'fungus' vs gold 'Fungi'. The number mismatch looks arbitrary, so no rule is proposed.

patch.reasoning: Two systematic gaps remain. (1) A bare list of real people is answered with a member, a relationship noun or a group label instead of the single shared country or realm; the current one-line rule is too weak and the agent ignored it. (2) Answers carry extra words: a product-type word after a brand, a habitat or type modifier before a species, or a title epithet that echoes the clue and varies between releases. These edits sharpen the existing list rule and add short brand/species and franchise-character rules that extend the delete-clue-words test. They are narrow and avoid the broad rewrites that were rejected in earlier steps.

edits.target: If the list is of real people, answer with the team, state or other entity they share.
edits.content: If the list is of real people (or a pair joined by '&' with no 'this'), the answer is the ONE proper-noun entity they all belong to: the country or realm a king, queen, prince or princess ruled or belongs to, the state they come from, or the team they play for. 'Ferdinand VII, Juan Carlos' -> 'Spain'; 'Princess Caroline & Princess Stephanie' -> 'Monaco'. Never answer with one person from the list (not 'Juan Carlos I'), a relationship or role word ('sisters', 'brothers', 'monarchs'), or a generic group label. Use the passages' repeated 'X of <Place>' / 'Prince of <Place>' phrasing to find the shared place.

The same goes for product-type words after a brand ('Hallmark', not 'Hallmark Cards'; 'Nike', not 'Nike Shoes') and for 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Airlines' or 'Records' when the bare brand names the company. For an animal or plant, give the plain common name that fits the clue's own descriptors ('lamprey', not 'sea lamprey', when the clue says 'freshwater'). Do not add a habitat, type or place modifier that comes only from a passage.

edits.target: - When the clue says only 'one of these' / 'this <generic noun>' and the answer is a common noun, give the plain common noun with no added modifiers:
edits.content: (Franchise/character clues: when the clue gives different epithets for one character in different years or releases ('In '84 he's a destroyer, in '82 he was just a barbarian'), the epithets are the clue's words, not the answer. Answer with the one name common to all of them ('Conan'), not a particular title that contains an epithet ('Conan the Destroyer').)
